causebase_summary: Biopixel Oceans Foundation Limited is an Australian marine research and education organisation operating on the Great Barrier Reef, Queensland. It tags and tracks marine animals in real time using the BioTracker platform, undertakes applied research on marine megafauna (including shark behaviour) and provides ecological information for fisheries management. The foundation maintains Oceanpedia, a multimedia library of short Great Barrier Reef video clips, produces videos and participates in streamed documentaries and media partnerships, and publishes journal articles and research collaborations. It also offers naming/sponsorship opportunities for individually tagged animals and reports tracking more than 1,000 animals currently being followed.

data.SummaryOfActivities: Biopixel Oceans Foundation continued conducting shark research around general movements and the impact of human and shark interaction for shark conservation and public safety. The program has been running since 2018 in the Whitsundays and 2021 at Northwest Island Capricorn Bunker group. Knowledge has been used to inform water users of shark behaviour (e.g. complementing Fisheries Queensland Shark Smart program) so they can make informed choices of when/how they undertake marine activities. BOF consolidated the previous 4 years of filed work on whale shark aggregation on the east coast of Australia. Producing a report for the QLD government threatened species department, and 4 scientific papers (resulting in 7 papers to date). Aa an extension, we discovered the first manta ray parturition site in Australia, located off Weipa in the Gulf of Carpentaria. Population studies of bull and tiger sharks on Australia s east coast continued. Under our lifeboat species banner, research assessing the health of species threatened internationally and believed to be healthy populations in Australia was conducted. This includes collecting data on population status and essential habitats for 20 species of shark and rays. Through the large-scale animal movement program BOF have electronically tagged >1300 animals and manage the largest QLD array ever deployed in QLD. BOF has worked with ReShark (ReWild) on the STAR project, collecting data and semen samples in Australia for breeding and restocking of leopard sharks in Indonesia https://www.reshark.org/star-project. We also facilitated the first expedition for ReShark to find and study Shark Rays, a highly threatened species that is the next candidate for the Rewilding program. BOF is also partnering with Queensland Fisheries, the University of Central Queensland, University of Sunshine Coast and game fishing clubs providing research to manage key commercial fishery species, such as black jewfish Protonibea diacanthaus and mud crabs and recreational fished species e.g. sailfish and dolphinfish. Three publications were produced in 2025. These activities helped BOF achieve its aim of supporting the protection and enhancement of our oceans through fostering a better understanding of shark behaviour and providing a data driven basis for determining shark policy. The continued whale shark and Omuras whale shark work continue to provide key findings for management in Australia and internationally. The Foundation shares live movement information of sharks to our public available biotracker https://biotracker.tv/. Biopixel work with Traditional owner groups, training them in scientific methods for understanding food web ecology and tracking totem species. In the last 2 years, seven post graduate students BOF staff have supervised or helped supervise have graduated. These public outputs support the Foundation's aim to foster education and a better understanding of the need for environmental protection and preservation.
